PHAR 180.title: Pharmaceutical Topics and Communication Seminar I
PHAR 180.description: Current topics in the Pharmaceutical Sciences and basic skills for a short presentation on a biological science topic.

PHAR 202.title: Biochemical Pharmacology
PHAR 202.description: Biochemical pharmacology including fundamental aspects of enzymology, biochemistry, enzyme kinetics, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics.
PHAR 202.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 112, BIOL_V 155, one of CHEM_V 111 or 121, CHEM_V 123, and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 120 or MATH_V 180

PHAR 203.title: Genetics for the Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHAR 203.description: Theoretical and practical knowledge of foundational concepts in genetics as they apply to the pharmaceutical sciences.

PHAR 204.title: Pharmaceutical Research
PHAR 204.description: Types of research scientists in Academia and Industry across the broad range of Pharmaceutical Science Disciplines.

PHAR 205.title: Clinical Epidemiology & Pharmaceutical Outcomes I
PHAR 205.description: Population-level study designs and critical appraisal skills in evidence evaluation, with a special emphasis on evidence-based pharmacy practice.

PHAR 280.title: Pharmaceutical Topics and Communication Seminar II
PHAR 280.description: Current topics in the Pharmaceutical and Biotechnology Industry and intermediate level skills for a short presentation.

PHAR 302.title: Pharmacokinetics
PHAR 302.description: Basic pharmacokinetic concepts: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. Evaluation of how drug physicochemistry, organism physiology, and pharmacogenetics affect pharmacokinetics.

PHAR 303.title: Nanomedicine
PHAR 303.description: Advanced nanomedicine concepts for drug packaging, delivery, and efficacy.

PHAR 304.title: Techniques in Molecular Biology and Pharmacology Theory and Laboratory
PHAR 304.description: Theoretical and practical knowledge of the foundational techniques used in pharmaceutical research in both Academic Research and the Pharmaceutical and Biotechnology Industries.
PHAR 304.prerequisiteText: CHEM_V 211, CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 235, PHAR_V 203, PHAR_V 204, MICB_V 212, and STAT_V 200

PHAR 305.title: Clinical Epidemiology & Pharmaceutical Outcomes II
PHAR 305.description: Population-level study designs and their critical appraisal skills in evidence evaluation, with a special emphasis on evidence-based pharmacy practice and the practical application of population-level data analysis and interpretation.

PHAR 306.title: Medicinal Chemistry of High-Impact Pharmaceuticals in Major Diseases
PHAR 306.description: Structure and mechanism of action of drugs used in the treatment of major chronic diseases: heart disease, cancer, lung disease, and diabetes.

PHAR 307.title: Analytical Sciences Theory and Laboratory
PHAR 307.description: Theoretical and practical knowledge of the analytical sciences commonly used in Academic Research as well as the Pharmaceutical and Biotechnology Industries.

PHAR 308.title: Systematic Pharmacology I
PHAR 308.description: Principles of pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics: drug action on infections, immune disorders, cancer, and major organ systems; beneficial and detrimental effects of drug action.

PHAR 309.title: Systematic Pharmacology II
PHAR 309.description: Principles of pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics: drug action on nervous and endocrine systems; beneficial and detrimental effects of drug action.

PHAR 370.title: Pharmaceutical Cases I
PHAR 370.description: Application and problem solving in the pharmaceutical sciences. Integration of knowledge and skills from multiple courses to problem solve authentic cases and problems of increasing complexity. Development of self-directed learning skills.

PHAR 380.title: Pharmaceutical Topics and Communication Seminar III
PHAR 380.description: Preliminary skills and concepts for planning, delivering and critiquing a scientific presentation using selected topics in the pharmaceutical sciences.

PHAR 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
PHAR 398.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Sciences Program. Pass/Fail.

PHAR 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
PHAR 399.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Sciences Program. Pass/Fail.

PHAR 415.title: Topics in Pharmaceutics and Biopharmaceutics
PHAR 415.description: A study of selected topics in the field of pharmaceutics and biopharmaceutics. Registration restricted. Permission of instructor required. .

PHAR 421.title: Precision Medicine
PHAR 421.description: Precision medicine approaches in research and medical practice to mitigate drug toxicity and improve drug efficacy.

PHAR 422.title: Pharmacoeconomics
PHAR 422.description: Evidence evaluation skills and understanding the role of, and the methods and principles used in, health economics and economic evaluation in healthcare, with a focus on health technology assessment studies.

PHAR 423.title: Statistical Methods and Data Science for Pharmaceutical Outcomes Research
PHAR 423.description: Principles of biostatistics, data science and epidemiology. Application of epidemiologic and statistical knowledge in the area of health outcomes.

PHAR 424.title: Financing and Therapeutics in the Canadian Health Care System
PHAR 424.description: Foundation in Canadian health care delivery systems and policies, with a focus on pharmaceutical policy and on comparison with other types of health care systems.

PHAR 425.title: Biologics
PHAR 425.description: Biologics as a therapeutic; how biologics are developed as drugs; synthesis and unique properties of biologics as drugs.

PHAR 426.title: Advanced Anesthetics and Analgesics
PHAR 426.description: Advanced concepts in anesthetic and analgesic drugs, their uses and abuses.

PHAR 427.title: Drug Structures in Medicinal Chemistry
PHAR 427.description: Therapeutically important privileged scaffolds and functional groups, and selectivity achieved through different chemical modifications.

PHAR 429.title: Adverse Drug Reactions
PHAR 429.description: Molecular and physiological basis of common adverse drug reactions (ADRs). ADRs in the context of current understanding of drug metabolism and pharmacogenetics. New approaches to prediction, detection and treatment.

PHAR 430.title: Biomolecular Pharmaceutical Chemistry
PHAR 430.description: Chemical principles and their application to drugs used to regulate enzyme activity. .

PHAR 431.title: Functional Foods
PHAR 431.description: Functional food concepts related to efficacy and safety; examples of bioactive component-disease relationships; natural health products; approval of functional food and health claims; the importance of clinical studies in support of efficacy for health claims; market determinants of functional foods.

PHAR 432.title: Toxicology
PHAR 432.description: Biochemical, cellular, and molecular processes that govern toxicity elicited by drugs and environmental toxins at the molecular, cellular, tissue, and organ system levels. Adverse drug reactions and precision medicine approaches to mitigate drug toxicity.

PHAR 433.title: Advanced Pharmacokinetics
PHAR 433.description: Polyexponential pharmacokinetics, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling, pharmacokinetic predictions, physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling and population-based pharmacokinetic modeling.

PHAR 470.title: Pharmaceutical Cases II
PHAR 470.description: Application of pharmaceutical sciences to authentic, complex cases spanning drug development and commercialization. Individual and team-based case analysis to strengthen problem-solving, critical thinking, professional communication and self-directed learning skills.

PHAR 480.title: Pharmaceutical Topics and Communication Seminar IV
PHAR 480.description: Senior level skills and concepts for planning, delivering and critiquing a scientific seminar using extended topics in the pharmaceutical sciences and beyond.

PHAR 485.title: Research Project
PHAR 485.description: Provides research experience equivalent to one full-time term of work on a defined research project in an area of pharmaceutical research.
PHAR 485.prerequisiteText: PHAR_V 302, PHAR_V 303, PHAR_V 304, PHAR_V 305, PHAR_V 306, PHAR_V 307, PHAR_V 308, and PHAR_V 370

PHAR 491.title: Honours Thesis
PHAR 491.description: Research project and production of a thesis document in an area of pharmaceutical research according to national/international standards.

PHAR 495.title: Practicum
PHAR 495.description: Provides practicum experience equivalent to one full-time term of work in a professional area of pharmaceutical research.
PHAR 495.prerequisiteText: PHAR_V 302, PHAR_V 303, PHAR_V 304, PHAR_V 305, PHAR_V 306, PHAR_V 307, PHAR_V 308, and PHAR_V 370

PHAR 496.title: Industry-Based Directed Studies in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHAR 496.description: Individual projects in an area of pharmaceutical research hosted at an industrial site.

PHAR 496.prerequisiteText: PHAR_V 204 and permission of the instructor. Preference will be given to students who have not completed PHAR_V 398

PHAR 497.title: Faculty-Based Directed Studies in Pharmaceutical Sciences
PHAR 497.description: Individual assignments involving library and laboratory investigation in an area of pharmaceutical research.

PHAR 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
PHAR 498.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Sciences Program. Pass/Fail.

PHAR 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
PHAR 499.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 13 weeks. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in the Bachelor of Pharmaceutical Sciences Program. Pass/Fail.

PHAR 502.title: Advanced Concepts in Pharmacokinetics
PHAR 502.description: Models of linear and dose-dependent systems in pharmacokinetics including sustained release, volumes of distribution, drug clearance, metabolite kinetics, multiple dosing and computer modelling. .

PHAR 510.title: Advanced Pharmaceutics I
PHAR 510.description: A study of physical and chemical properties of pharmaceutical systems with emphasis on formulation and preparative aspects.

PHAR 511.title: Advanced Pharmaceutics II
PHAR 511.description: A study of problems in pharmaceutics with emphasis on biopharmaceutical aspects.

PHAR 515.title: Nanomedicines
PHAR 515.description: Nano-sized drug delivery systems and their interactions with biological systems.

PHAR 516.title: Polymeric Drug and Protein Delivery
PHAR 516.description: Advances in polymer-based drug delivery systems. .

PHAR 517.title: Lipid-Based Drug Delivery
PHAR 517.description: Advances in lipophilic drug delivery systems. .

PHAR 518.title: Diagnostic Imaging and Radiopharmaceuticals
PHAR 518.description: Radiation-related, optical, and other imaging methods (SPECT, PET, CT, MRI, microscopy, ultrasound) and their application in research. .

PHAR 520.title: Applied Omics Science for Drug Discovery and Development
PHAR 520.description: General principles of genomics, proteomics, glycomics, and metabolomics; advanced functional omics techniques and their applications in pharmaceutical research.

PHAR 521.title: Basic Theory & Practice of Scanning Electron Microscopy and Dynamic Light Scattering
PHAR 521.description: Sample preparation; standard & advanced imaging techniques; image interpretation & quantification, applications in pharmaceutical research.

PHAR 522.title: Basic Theory and Practice of Liquid Chromatography - Mass Spectrometry in Pharmaceutical Research
PHAR 522.description: Fundamental and practical knowledge and skills to run liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry.

PHAR 523.title: Basic Theory & Practice of Isothermal Titration Calorimetry
PHAR 523.description: Isothermal titration calorimetry thermodynamic concepts and practical applications in measuring molecular interactions.

PHAR 524.title: Cell Culture and New Biomedical Approaches
PHAR 524.description: Basic cell culture techniques and novel insights into alternative methods in biomedical research.

PHAR 525.title: Pharmaceutical Research Techniques I
PHAR 525.description: Spectroscopic, GC, HPLC, LCMS and NMR analytical techniques for drug analysis, pharmacokinetics and metabolism. .

PHAR 526.title: Pharmaceutical Research Techniques II
PHAR 526.description: Immunological assays, capillary and gel electrophoresis, radioisotope techniques, PET, peptide analysis and receptor binding studies. .

PHAR 540.title: Topics in Pharmacology
PHAR 540.description: Lectures and supervised studies in selected areas of pharmacology. Enrolment restricted.

PHAR 541.title: Drug Metabolism and Toxicology
PHAR 541.description: The biotransformation of drugs, pesticides, carcinogens and other foreign chemicals in animals and humans. The biochemical mechanisms responsible, particularly the cytochrome P-450 mono-oxygenases, will be emphasized. The formation of toxic reactive metabolites and their effects will be discussed. Enrolment restricted.

PHAR 542.title: Central Nervous System Pharmacology
PHAR 542.description: A course comprised of lectures, assigned readings and reports on selected topics dealing with drug actions in the central nervous system. Given in alternate years. Permission of instructor required.

PHAR 543.title: Advanced Laboratory in Pharmacology
PHAR 543.description: A laboratory course giving instruction in the methods and techniques used in pharmacological research. Registration limited. .

PHAR 545.title: Cardiovascular Pharmacology
PHAR 545.description: A course composed of lectures, assigned readings and conferences dealing with aspects of drug actions and cardiovascular function. Topics include the role of adenylate cyclase in cardiac function, the role of calcium in myocardial contractility and the effect of drugs on myocardial and vascular function. Enrolment restricted. Given in alternate years.

PHAR 546.title: Etiology of Diabesity, from Cell to Society
PHAR 546.description: Advanced course on pathophysiology and patient care for obesity and diabetes focusing on healthcare quality improvement, patient safety and optimising outcomes.

PHAR 548.title: M.Sc. Seminar
PHAR 548.description: Attendance at regular seminars throughout the session and presentation of one or more papers on selected topics.

PHAR 560.title: Advanced Economic Evaluation in Health Care
PHAR 560.description: Economic evaluation of health technologies, considering, in detail, the policy context for the use of economic evaluation.

PHAR 561.title: Pharmacoepidemiology
PHAR 561.description: Principles and applications of pharmacoepidemiology. Practical skills in designing, conducting, and appraising studies of medications in large populations.

PHAR 598.description: Permission of the supervisor required. Pass/Fail.

PHAR 648.title: Seminar for Ph.D. Students
PHAR 648.description: Attendance at regular seminars throughout the session and presentation of one or more papers on selected topics.
